title: Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford & Davante Adams discuss injury updates, keys to beating the Bills, limiting penalties & more
headline: Rams' injury report looks manageable: Aaron Donald, Colby Parkinson and Jaylen Watson are limited and expected to ramp up, while Davante Adams only had a veteran rest day.
summary: McVay opened with the Thursday injury report: Jaylen Watson, Aaron Donald and Colby Parkinson were limited, Josaiah Stewart (groin), Quentin Lake (hip), Nate Landman (shoulder) and one more player (hamstring, name garbled) did not practice, and Davante Adams had a veteran rest day. He hopes the three limited players are ready for the Bills game and said the plan is to build them up through the week, with Donald's back response the thing to watch. He had no specific update on Myles Garrett beyond good rehab progress and good meeting-room work, and he has not decided whether to open his practice window. McVay called the Lake and Landman absences a snap-count management move and said Lake's hip came from an odd fall. He praised Trent McDuffie's consistency, Byron Young's improvement and humility, and Matthew Stafford's performance in key moments, but said the team has too many penalties, especially in the kicking game and in scoring position. He also covered the new kickoff rules, Joe Brady being the league's youngest head coach, and the signing of Eric Kendricks to the practice squad for defensive depth. In his own session Stafford said he needs to be more consistent, praised Josh Allen, and talked up the Bills' defense under coordinator Jim Leonhard.

injuries.detail: Back issue. Limited Thursday. McVay hopes he plays and said everything is progressing in the right direction.
Limited Thursday and progressing very positively. The team will be careful with his reps.
Limited Thursday. McVay wants to see how he feels and mentioned a shoulder harness, so a shoulder issue is likely but not confirmed.
Did not practice with a groin injury.
Did not practice with a minor hip injury from an awkward fall. McVay called it snap-count management and said he is tough.
Did not practice with a shoulder injury. McVay said the team is being smart given his heavy snap count.
Veteran rest day, not an injury designation.
McVay said rehab is progressing and he looks good in meetings, but had no specific update and had not decided on opening a practice window.

signals.claim: Aaron Donald is expected to play in the next game if his back responds well this week.
signals.note: Limited rather than out is a good sign, but his availability depends on how the back responds.

signals.claim: Parkinson will build up through the week with managed reps and be ready for the game.
signals.note: He is trending toward playing at TE, though his workload may be monitored.
signals.quote: Colby's progressing really in a very positive direction.

signals.claim: Watson will be wrapped up through the week and should be ready if he progresses accordingly.
signals.note: Status depends on how he feels, and the transcript is unclear about the specific injury.
signals.quote: So want to see how Jalen feels.

signals.note: McVay had no concrete timetable or update on a return to practice.

signals.claim: Lake's missed practice is precautionary and tied to his snap count.
signals.note: The hip issue is described as minor, so he is a low-risk watch for IDP.
signals.quote: We're just being smart with him.

signals.claim: Stafford remains the unquestioned starting QB.
signals.note: McVay praised his late-game performance and steadiness, so his job is secure.
signals.quote: there's nobody that I'd rather have leading us.

topics.detail: McVay is unhappy with the number of flags, especially procedural and judgment penalties, kicking-game penalties and offensive penalties in scoring position. He is emphasizing cleanup but does not want players to play less aggressively.
The new kickoff rules matter a lot for late-half and late-game decisions because of the yardage at stake and the range kickers now convert from.
The Rams signed Kendricks to the practice squad for defensive depth. McVay praised his experience and his understanding of the defense.

Stafford said the offense improved in the final two drives by staying ahead of the chains and avoiding penalties. He singled out Tyler Higbee ('awesome') and Kyren Williams (great in the passing and run game). These were Stafford's comments, not McVay's.
Stafford said the Bills have a physical, disruptive front and a back end that changes looks at the snap under coordinator Jim Leonhard. He called Josh Allen one of the most talented QBs in the NFL.
McVay called McDuffie consistent and a 'total stud', and praised Byron Young's improvement every year and his impact this season.
